audience_name: Lean support team lead at a scaling software company

dossier.audience_name: Lean support team lead at a scaling software company
dossier.orientation: Help Scout is a shared-inbox help desk with an AI Answers add-on that replies to common customer questions and hands the rest to the human agents already working in that inbox.

setup_conditions: AI Answers must be deployed with Beacon and pointed at Docs or other knowledge sources (E23).
Accuracy upkeep runs through Improvements/Suggested Improvements review from inside conversations (E26, E27).
AI Answers is an add-on billed at $0.75 per AI resolution as defined by Help Scout (R3, R4).

Teams coming from Zendesk use the built-in Import2 for ticket history and customer profiles, request a separate team-assisted tool for knowledge-base articles, and manually recreate macros and triggers (R5).
unverified_requirements: Absorbing repetitive questions without putting the team through a new, disruptive support stack when the team is not already on Help Scout
decision_gaps: Does Help Scout's own documentation state whether AI Answers replies to inbound email conversations in the shared inbox, or only in-app through Beacon?
Does Help Scout document a migration path for teams coming from a plain shared mailbox (e.g. Google Workspace) rather than Zendesk?

unverified_requirement_basis.Absorbing repetitive questions without p: without adding staff or forcing the team through a new, disruptive support stack

defining_need_fit.caveat: The non-disruptive claim is documented only for a customer already working inside Help Scout (E22-adjacent framing in E23/E26), while the only documented inbound migration path (R5, Zendesk) states no timeline and requires manual recreation of macros and triggers, so the whole stated need is supported in components rather than end to end.
defining_need_fit.why: Shared-inbox triage (E16), AI handling of simple repetitive questions with human handoff (E18, E23, E21) and a measured deflection result at one lean software team (R6) are documented, but adoption without a disruptive stack change is established only for existing Help Scout teams.

ranked_relevance.why: States the mechanism the need asks for: AI Answers handling common questions instantly alongside workflow automations.
Documents how AI Answers behaves in Beacon, including its knowledge sources and the handoff to a human when needed.
The only figured result for a lean software support team, with deflection climbing past 10% and peaking at 15.46% in August 2025.
Describes the shared-inbox queue, customer context and behind-the-scenes collaboration that the audience's triage workflow runs on.
Explains the documented upkeep mechanism behind AI accuracy: adding missing context from a conversation without rewriting help articles.
Defines what counts as an AI resolution, which bounds what 'AI absorbed the question' means in billing terms.
Per-resolution pricing at $0.75 is the concrete cost of the capacity being added instead of a hire.
Documents the Zendesk import path and its stated exceptions, which is the only licensed material on arriving without rebuilding everything.

problem_fits.caveat: Single-source review with unknown publication date, so it confirms the workflow signal rather than a current, corroborated pain.
problem_fits.why: The shared-inbox queue with collaboration and resolution tracking described in P1 is the documented capability in E16.

segment_objections.objection: A deflection rate in the 10-15% range will not free enough capacity to stand in for the agent we lost.
segment_objections.answer: The documented result is one lean software team climbing past 10% and peaking at 15.46% in August 2025 while weekly AI-handled conversations grew from 36 to nearly 300, with the stated intent being that AI takes the simple questions rather than replacing the team.

segment_objections.objection: Getting this AI means moving our support stack, which is the disruption we are trying to avoid.
segment_objections.answer: AI Answers runs inside the Help Scout inbox the team already works in, and for Zendesk teams the built-in Import2 brings ticket history and customer profiles across, though the knowledge base needs a separate team-assisted tool and macros and triggers must be recreated by hand.

evidence.claim: Help Scout's shared inbox gives all teammates access to the queue, letting them see customer context, collaborate behind the scenes, and follow conversations to resolution.
evidence.verbatim: Help Scout’s shared inbox makes that easy. All teammates have access to the queue and can see customer context, collaborate behind the scenes, and follow conversations to resolution.

evidence.claim: AI Answers handles common customer questions instantly, and workflow automations help the team stay organized and responsive.
evidence.verbatim: AI Answers handles common questions instantly, while workflow automations help their team stay organized and responsive.

evidence.claim: eCatholic's Director of Onboarding & Success, Luke Tristani, said AI Answers isn't meant to replace support teams but to let AI handle simple questions so the team can create 'wow moments' for customers.
evidence.verbatim: We’re not looking to replace support teams with AI, but if we can let AI answer the simple questions, it frees us up to create ‘wow moments’ for customers.

evidence.claim: Luke evaluated other AI vendors — Zoom, Maven, and Intercom — and found those bolt-on tools required major process changes, whereas AI Answers lives inside Help Scout where the team already works.
evidence.verbatim: After weighing various AI vendors like Zoom, Maven, and Intercom, Luke found those bolt-on tools required major process changes. AI Answers stood out because it lives where the team already works, in Help Scout.

context.subject: AI Answers vs Zoom, Maven, Intercom
context.limitations: Rival claim attributed to customer's evaluation, not independently verified.

evidence.claim: Inside Beacon, AI Answers provides instant, in-app answers with a smooth handoff to a human when needed, drawing on Docs and other knowledge sources, and can be instantly improved with suggestions from recent email conversations.
evidence.verbatim: Inside Beacon, AI Answers provides instant, in-app answers with a smooth handoff to a human when needed. It draws on Docs and other knowledge sources, can be instantly improved with suggestions from recent email conversations, and captures eCatholic’s friendly, approachable tone to stay on-brand.

evidence.claim: With Improvements, teams can quickly add missing context right from a conversation without rewriting help articles, and Help Scout's AI learns directly from that feedback to make the next answer more accurate and on-brand.
evidence.verbatim: With Improvements, Luke’s team can quickly add missing context right from a conversation. There’s no need to rewrite help articles. Help Scout’s AI learns directly from that feedback, which means the next answer is more accurate and on-brand.

evidence.claim: Help Scout bills AI Answers (Envoy) per resolution, not per conversation or per reply, at $0.75 per resolution

context.subject: Help Scout AI Answers / Envoy add-on
context.claim_scope: all plans (Standard, Plus, Pro) per the pricing/feature comparison table

evidence.claim: Help Scout defines a billable AI resolution as a single conversation resolved by AI without human assistance and without further customer escalation
evidence.verbatim:
A resolution is a single conversation that is resolved by AI Answers without human assistance.

A resolution is counted only if the customer receives an AI response and doesn’t use escalation, search the knowledge base, ask more questions, or indicate that they need more help.

context.subject: Help Scout AI Answers billing unit definition
context.claim_scope: AI Answers / Envoy add-on, all plans
context.conditions: customer must not escalate, search KB, ask more questions, or request more help
context.limitations: only one resolution is billed per conversation even with multiple AI replies

evidence.claim: Help Scout documents an import path for moving an existing shared inbox (from Zendesk) via its built-in Import2 feature, covering ticket history and customer profiles, with knowledge-base import handled by a separate team-assisted tool; no specific timeline/duration is stated anywhere in the article.
evidence.verbatim: Help Scout's built in Import2 feature allows you to import your entire ticket history (and the customer profiles associated with those tickets) from Zendesk into Help Scout.

context.subject: Help Scout Import2 feature for migrating from Zendesk
context.claim_scope: Migration path specifically for teams moving from Zendesk to Help Scout
context.conditions: Applies to ticket/customer data; knowledge base articles require contacting Help Scout for a different import tool and instructions, and should not be run through Import2 to avoid duplicate data.
context.limitations: No timeline, duration, or completion estimate for the import process is stated anywhere in this article; Macros/Triggers are not imported and must be manually recreated.

evidence.claim: eCatholic, a software company with a 'lean support team,' reports an AI Answers deflection rate that climbed past 10% and peaked at 15.46% in August 2025, growing from 36 conversations handled in the first week to nearly 300 per week by August.
evidence.verbatim: Their deflection rate, which Luke once hoped might reach 10%, has consistently climbed past that mark, peaking at 15.46% in August 2025, their highest yet.

context.subject: eCatholic (software company serving churches, schools, and ministries) using Help Scout AI Answers
context.claim_scope: Deflection rate for one named software customer; team size is described only as 'lean support team,' not quantified as 2-10 agents
context.conditions: Measured after adopting AI Answers inside an existing Help Scout/Beacon setup, starting early 2025
context.limitations: The source does not state the exact number of support agents (no 2-10 agent figure given), so this cannot be confirmed as specific to a 2-10 agent team; it is a single customer's result, not a general SaaS benchmark.

verified_product_questions: Absorbing repetitive questions without forcing a disruptive support-stack change for a team that is not already working in Help Scout
Does public documentation state a migration/import path and timeline for moving an existing shared inbox into Help Scout?
Is there a documented AI Answers deflection or volume-spike figure for a software/SaaS team of 2-10 agents specifically?
